kartikpur-zamindar-bari.desc: Kartikpur in Naria upazila was once part of the Bikrampur zamindari, and the family that ruled here traced its line to a Mughal commander, Fateh Muhammad. Locally it is called Chowdhury Bari. A decorated two-storey house remains, and the road up to it is lined with carved pillars eight to ten feet tall, many now broken. There is also a pond with a brick bathing ghat. Descendants of the zamindars still live in the house, which is worn but standing.
blocks: How to get there
From Shariatpur town take a CNG or auto toward Naria and on to Kartikpur village; ask for the Chowdhury Bari.
Good to know
This is a private home, so ask the family's permission before entering the grounds and be respectful.

monohar-bazar-hilsa-fair.desc: At Monohar Bazar in Shariatpur Sadar upazila, a traditional fair is held at the start of the Bangla month of Magh, usually in mid-January. Families buy hilsa in pairs, a custom tied to faith and good fortune for the new month, along with sweets, toys and rural snacks. Hundreds of people come for the day. It is a lively glimpse of a living rural custom.

glance: 95 km to Shariatpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
dhanuka-manasa-bari.desc: In Dhanuka village, close to Shariatpur town, stands a cluster of old buildings known as Manasa Bari, associated with the family of the Sanskrit scholar Mayurbhatta. Surviving structures include Kali, Durga and Manasa temples, a nahabat khana for musicians and a building that once housed a Sanskrit tol. Locals date the complex back several centuries. It is in poor repair, which adds to its atmosphere but means you should tread carefully.
blocks: How to get there
Rickshaw from Shariatpur town, about 10 minutes.
Good to know
Some structures are unstable; stay out of cracked or cordoned areas.

jajira-padma-bridge-view.desc: The Padma Bridge, opened in 2022, crosses the river from Mawa in Munshiganj to Jajira in Shariatpur. On the Jajira side, the riverbank and nearby roads give clear views of the long steel truss and its piers marching across the water. In the evening, lights come on along the deck and fishing boats drift underneath. Many visitors from Dhaka now cross just to see it from this bank.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Dhaka across the bridge to Jajira, then a local auto to the riverside.
Good to know
Stopping on the bridge is not permitted; enjoy the view from designated spots on the bank.

glance: Fish markets and eateries in Naria, Jajira and Gosairhat
shariatpur-hilsa.desc: With the Padma on its north and the Meghna to the east, Shariatpur is surrounded by some of the best hilsa water in the country. Fishing ghats around Naria and Gosairhat are busy in the season. Cooks fry the fish crisp, cook it in mustard gravy, or wrap it in banana leaf to steam. It is at its richest in the monsoon.

palong-bazar-rasgolla.desc: In Palong bazar, the main market of Shariatpur town, one family sweet shop has made rasgolla since 1950, and it still makes up most of their sales. The sweets are soft, light and not too sugary. The shop also makes sandesh, rasmalai and lal mohon. Locals bring boxes when visiting relatives.

glance: Home kitchens and winter pitha fairs
shariatpur-bibikhana-pitha.desc: Bibikhana is a cake-like pitha made from rice flour, milk, eggs, coconut and date-palm gur, slow-cooked until golden on top. It is popular across Bangladesh but is a point of pride in Shariatpur, where it is listed among the district's notable dishes. It is a winter treat, often made when guests visit. Ask at a homestay or local eatery to try it.

burirhat-mosque.desc: The Burirhat mosque began in 1907 as a thatched prayer house built by a local trader, and was rebuilt in brick in stages until it took its present form in 1935. The design was by Aftab Uddin Munshi, and the building is covered in ornate decoration, with walls more than three feet thick. A tall minaret was added beside the main gate in the 1990s and the hall was enlarged in 2015; it now holds about a thousand worshippers. The mosque stands on five acres of waqf land with an Eidgah, a pond and a market.
blocks: How to get there
From Shariatpur town take a CNG or bus toward Chandpur along the Shariatpur–Chandpur road and get off at Burirhat bazar (Rudrakar union); the mosque is at the bazar's south-west edge.
Good to know
Dress modestly and avoid Friday midday prayers if you want to look around. Rudrakar Math is close by and makes a good pairing.

glance: 95 km to Shariatpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
rudrakar-math.desc: Rudrakar Math is an old Hindu memorial temple tower in Rudrakar union of Shariatpur Sadar upazila. Built of brick in the tall, tapering style common to Bengal's zamindar-era maths, it rises above the surrounding trees and fields. It sees few visitors from outside the district. Combine it with Dhanuka Manasa Bari for a half-day heritage loop.
blocks: How to get there
CNG or auto from Shariatpur town to Rudrakar; ask locally for the math.

glance: 95 km to Shariatpur by road, 3–4 hours by bus or car
sureshwar-darbar-sharif.desc: The Sureshwar Darbar in Naria upazila is the shrine of a Sufi saint and the centre of a devotional order with followers across Bangladesh. Its domed shrine and courtyards fill with pilgrims during the annual urs, when devotional songs continue late into the night. At other times it is calm and contemplative. Visitors of all backgrounds are generally welcome if respectful.
blocks: How to get there
Bus or CNG from Shariatpur town to Naria, then an auto to Sureshwar.
Good to know
Dress modestly and remove shoes where required.
